title: FREE TRAINING ON BUSINESS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT BY ELISHA FOUNDATION
description: Following the "How to End Poverty" workshop, it became evident that individuals were eager to transform their circumstances by...
story:
Following the "How to End Poverty" workshop, it became evident that individuals were eager to transform their circumstances by securing employment opportunities and establishing their businesses. Recognizing this need and the potential for impactful change, we have introduced the Business and Financial Management class. We aim to provide participants with the essential skills and knowledge necessary to navigate the complexities of business and finance confidently, thereby facilitating their journey toward overcoming poverty effortlessly.
The Elisha Foundation is excited to announce a unique opportunity for individuals passionate about ending poverty in our community. We are organizing free training sessions on business and financial (money) management exclusively for those who attended the "How to End Poverty" workshop. At Elisha Foundation, we believe in equipping individuals with the necessary tools and knowledge to thrive in their endeavors.
 During these training sessions, participants will delve into the fundamental principles of business and money management. Topics covered will include:
Basic principles of business and money management.
Digital strategies to enhance sales in business.
Financial planning and saving techniques.
Investment strategies for long-term financial growth.
And much more!
The Elisha Foundation is deeply committed to ending poverty in our community. By providing free training on essential business and financial management skills, we aim to empower individuals to break the cycle of poverty and achieve financial independence. We believe that everyone deserves the opportunity to thrive, and through education and support, we can make this vision a reality.
 If you attended the "How to End Poverty" workshop and are eager to learn more about business and financial management, we encourage you to participate in these training sessions. 
The training sessions take place every Thursday throughout May and June and it is absolutely free.
Together, let's take meaningful steps towards ending poverty and building a prosperous future for all.

title: CONGRATULATIONS TO ALL THE BRILLIANT MINDS WHO HAVE SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETED THE THREE-MONTH, TUITION-FREE WEB DEVELOPMENT COURSE
description: Earlier this year, we proudly announced our commitment to providing free coding classes throughout the year.
story:
Earlier this year, we proudly announced our commitment to providing free coding classes throughout the year. Staying true to our promise, we commenced the first cohort on February 5th, 2024, with an initial enrollment of approximately 41 eager students. Following a rigorous screening process, 21 dedicated individuals were accepted into the program, marking the beginning of their educational journey.
After three months of intensive classes, a remarkable 12 students demonstrated unwavering dedication and successfully completed the course. These talented individuals were divided into three groups, each tasked with designing innovative projects: a quiz app, a weather app, and a music app. Despite facing challenges along the way, 11 of these students ultimately graduated, showcasing their remarkable commitment and perseverance.
We extend our heartfelt appreciation to our esteemed partners, Mr. Samuel Kelechi, and our dedicated facilitators, Kennedy Nkem, Suliton Olalere, and Mazi UjahCollinsz, whose unwavering support and expertise made this initiative possible. Your thorough teachings and incredible dedication have truly made a lasting impact.
We would also like to express our gratitude to the Elisha Foundation for their steadfast commitment to community empowerment and for prioritizing the needs of Ajegunle, Lagos State.
It is evident that through our collective efforts, we are actively working towards the eradication of poverty in Ajegunle, Lagos State

title: HOW TO END POVERTY
description: Based on the World Bank,  poverty rates in Nigeria have increased to 46per cent in 2023. Over 104 million Nigerians are poor and living in abject poverty.
story:
Over the past few decades, the world has made great strides in the fight against poverty. 
However,  there is still much work to be done. 
Poverty is a state or condition in which one lacks the financial resources essential for a certain standard of living. It is also about not having enough money to meet basic needs including food, clothing and shelter.
Based on the World Bank,  poverty rates in Nigeria have increased to 46per cent in 2023. Over 104 million Nigerians are poor and living in abject poverty. 
We need to be self-reliant because if we keep waiting for the government we will end up waiting in vain. 
Barack Obama once said "If poverty is a disease that infects the entire community in the form of unemployment and violence, failing schools and broken homes, then we can’t just treat those symptoms in isolation. We have to heal that entire community.” 
This is why this conference is designed to enlighten you on how to curb this poverty that is eating deep into our economy despite our natural resources. 
It is a 3-day mind-blowing conference. Set a reminder, and mark the dates on your calendar.  You are going to draw from the fountain of knowledge ... 
Anticipate!

title: OLODI APAPA PRIMARY SCHOOL INTERHOUSE SPORT
description: Yesterday, representatives of the Elisha Foundation were present at the inter-house sports ceremony of the Olodi Apapa Primary School
story:
Getting involved in community welfare is one of our priorities.
We do not only support with donations but we also make sure our presence counts.
Yesterday, representatives of the Elisha Foundation were present at the inter-house sports ceremony of the Olodi Apapa Primary School. 
The competition started with a march past, school relay, parents relay, etc.
In the beginning, Pink House showed great enthusiasm, their match past was well organized and they were all in accordance but when it got to other activities they failed. 
Yellow House came first at the end of the competition with 7 gold medals and 4 bronze and seeing the joy in the faces of these kids brings fulfillment to us. 
Our delight is in making lives and communities better and we are happy they are been fulfilled.

title: HELP US SPONSOR A STUDENT
description: At the beginning of school sessions, we get lots of letters of sponsorship and support from various students, ranging from primary school students...
story:
At the beginning of school sessions, we get lots of letters of sponsorship and support from various students, ranging from primary school students, secondary school students, and tertiary and university students. You all know that Elisha Foundation has the interest of the community at heart, we usually do a lot of work behind the camera before bringing it to the public. 
We received lots of requests from parents and students who cannot afford to pay their admissions and tuition fees.
Elisha Foundation is doing the little (which is not little)we can but we are beginning to get exhausted,  this is why we brought this here.
We want everyone to be a part of the "Sponsor a Student" project. We urge you all to please help us fulfill the dreams of these young ones, let's not dash their hope and future, they are the leaders of tomorrow.
Elizabeth (not her real name) was one of the students who came for help, she is a student at Ogun State University studying Science Laboratory Technology popularly known as SLT. She needed our help to pay her year 2 school fees. 
We requested her school details and checked her first semester results, which is our usual routine, it was very bad with lots of Pass, but what differentiated her from others was that she told us outright that her first semester results were bad because she resumed school late, she missed loads of test and attendance. She assured us that her second-semester results would be different. 
When the results came out, it was very good, and her CGP improved. 
We were very pleased and this ginger us to pay her tuition. 
We hope this story inspires you to join the help sponsor a student campaign. 
PS: This is 1 out of hundreds of people we have helped to pay their school fees. We are urging everyone to support the "help sponsor a student project" 
With your help we will do more, your #500,  #1000 will go a long way to put a smile on the faces of these students.
The "change" we are all clamoring for is here, let it begin with you!
Sponsor a Student back to school.
Send your support to the account details below;
 Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation,
 3150003919, Ecobank.

story:
Desmond Tutu once said " Do your little bit of good where you are; it's those little bits of good put together that overwhelm the world " 
Our little way of doing good is to fulfill our commitments, we promised the Ajegunle spelling bee finalists that they would be allowed to learn to code. 
True to our promise, we embarked on a one-month coding class and it was attended by over 80 students from different schools. 
We are happy that we are fulfilling our purpose which is to make lives and communities better. 
A big shout out to our esteemed partner Mr Samuel Kelechi, who is a maven when it comes to tech. 
We also took time to talk to these kids about child sexual abuse, we want these generations to be free from abuse so that they can concentrate fully on their studies.
We taught them the basic pants rules for kids which are...
P; Private parts are private, nobody is permitted to touch them.
A; Always remember, your body is yours and only yours
N; No means no, don't give in to pressure
T; There are no secrets from mummy and daddy. If anyone tries anything always tell mummy and daddy.
S; Say something so I can do something about it/ Speak up.
Thanks to our speakers, Miss Titilope Olumofin and Miss Vanessa Linda Gakwe, your contribution to the community cannot be overemphasized.
Watch out for our quarterly coding classes next year 2024!

title: SECOND EDITION OF THE CRUSADE FOR AWARENESS.
description: Crusade for Awareness is a yearly event organised by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation popularly known as...
story:
Crusade for Awareness is a yearly event organised by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation popularly known as Elisha Foundation. This is the second edition and the aim of these events is to influence people's thoughts towards Skills acquisition, healthy living, Sexual abuse and rape, domestic violence, and other vices. This year's event was held for 2 days.
We invited terrific speakers to speak on the aforementioned topics to audiences online and offline, we believe that if the community thrives, individuals will grow and the crime rate will reduce.
At Elisha Foundation, we pay close attention to the development of our community, we want the good of every resident both young and old.
Our mission is to create a platform where every citizen excels. 
The issue of domestic violence and sexual abuse is becoming disturbing and needs to be addressed instantaneously.
Sexual abuse and rape should be taken seriously. Abusers/rapists should face the consequences of their actions.
The community cannot thrive if there are rapists, pedophiles, etc going about perpetuating their evil deeds. 
During these year's events, we gave the attendance opportunity to learn skills while we sponsored it, we also gave out ladies' menstruation pads and cleaning items as a little empowerment to our community.
We are using these mediums to solicit donations and support to be able to do more for our community, We call on government and private bodies, and stakeholders to please partner with us, and help us to better our community.

Indeed it is good to be good to others because happiness truly comes from being good to others.

title: GRAND FINALE OF THE AJEGUNLE SPELLING BEE
description: The Ajegunle Spelling Bee competition was not only about spelling, the parents and guardian of the spellers were spoken to by Miss Yetunde...
story:
The second edition of the Ajegunle Spelling Bee competition ended with lots of jubilation.
The competition started with the host Miss Titilope Olumofin telling the audience what the Ajegunle Spelling Bee competition stands to achieve, then the co host Mr. Sunday Sanni spoke about the many events Elisha Foundation has organised to help empower not only youths but every individual living in Ajegunle.
The competition was an undeniable battle of words as the spellers from each category showed they had all prepared wholeheartedly. 
The judge's panellists consist of Mr Scepter Ashogbon, Miss Vanessa Gakwe and HRM Williams Olamide, their genuine opinion and patience towards the spellers cannot be overemphasised. 
The Ajegunle Spelling Bee competition was not only about spelling, the parents and guardian of the spellers were spoken to by Miss Yetunde Olaniyan, she talked about the values of education while our beautiful queen and her court talked about parental  involvement in their children education and importance of being educated.
Winners of the first edition of the Ajegunle Spelling Bee competition were invited too to talk about their scholarship scheme.
After rounds and rounds of spelling, Glorious Ifejika came top at the lower primary after spelling the word "Contentment".
Toluwalase Asemudara came top at the upper primary after spelling the word "Animosity"
Rukayat Yusuf came top in the junior category after spelling the word "Camaraderie"
Dominic Onowho came top in the senior category after spelling the word "paraphernalia"
Each of these top spellers won a scholarship of 250,000 to further their education.
All the 80 finalists were gifted merchandise school bags, advance oxford dictionaries, pencils, biro, erasers and water bottles.
Not only that, all the  80 finalists will have the opportunity to get tech skills.
We will be partnering with "The Curve African" to help them get a skill in coding.
The feeling of winning a 250,000 naira scholarship for your education is a thing to be delighted and proud of.
The economy of the country is nothing to write home about and it is affecting all other sectors, talk of school fees, house rent, fuel etc.
Elisha Foundation is doing all it can to secure the future of the next generation, either in entertainment, education, individual development or empowerment.
Elisha Foundation will continue to make lives and communities better

title: GRAND FINALE OF THE MISS ELISHA BEAUTY PAGEANT
description: The pageantry ended with so much jubilation as Joy Nwangu won the Miss Elisha Foundation 2023
story:
The event started with an opening prayer by Mr Tomoloju Olamide, we all know that whatever is committed into the hands of  God ends with great success.
The whole event was graced by distinguished ladies and men of class.
The likes of Ward E councillor, Mr Arole, Mr Emmanuel, Mr Sunday and many more.
The judge's panellists consist of Mr Prince Ogaga Wowo, the CEO of Kobis multidimensional projects Ltd, Miss Gift Wisdom, CEO of Giftcheria Makeover ,Miss Queensley, CEO of Poshquin fashion house and lastly Mr Victor Ekeleme, he is a brand infleuncer , a model and a chaperone, his contribution to the Miss Elisha beauty pageant cannot be undermined, he taught the contestants their routine catwalk.
They gave their unbiased judgment wholeheartedly.
The judges are the definition of community builders, they deserve our accolades.
We also have panellists who spoke on women's empowerment, contraceptives and sexual abuse and rape.
This women's speech was insightful and morale-boosting.
Most of the quest artist happens to be the winners of our Talent Expo and they gave us a great performance.
The event ended with lots of jubilation as Joy Nwangu was crowned Miss Elisha Foundation Beauty Pageant 2023, she is enthusiastic, intelligent, outspoken, confident and beautiful. She was awarded #500,000 as the winning prize. 
Bolanle Olaniyan won the 1st runner-up, she is brilliant, smart, and eloquent and her charisma during her spoken words was top-notch. She was awarded #300,000 while...
Temitope Atanda won the 2nd runner-up with winning prize money of #200,000. The chocolate skin girl wowed the judges with her catwalks, smiles, body carriage and charisma.
Cynthia Johnson won the best dress, her dress was designed by her mom. Mrs Juliet Johnson was awarded #50,000 for her craftsmanship. The dress was simply elegant.
Joy Nwangu, the winner of the Miss Elisha Foundation beauty pageant also won best make-up.
Priscilla Ijomah won the best hairdo, her hair was beautiful. 
Mr Prince Ogaga Wowo also offer to add a 10,000 cash prize to the best make-up, best dressed and best hair.
All the other seven contestants were awarded #100,000 each as compensation for being part of the pageant.
Buyers of the contestant's charity tickets were also picked randomly and 10 of them won #10,000 each.
We want to appreciate Esfam Benin Republic University for offering the Contestants and every other student from Elisha Foundation a scholarship to their university. 
Esfam Benin Republic University is one of the best schools,  it is well-accredited by the Ministry of Higher Education in Benin Republic and also by the Ministry of Education in Nigeria. Their graduates go through the national youth service (NYSC) program immediately after graduation. 
Also, we want to appreciate Kobis Multidimensional Projects Ltd for offering the Contestants 6 months of photography training for free and also offering the winner of the Miss Elisha Foundation beauty 4 months photoshoot.
#AHeartOfGratitude 
#misselishafoundation

title: Audition for the second edition of Talent Expo
description: Talent they say is your gateway out of poverty if you hone it. What that means is that you have to be persistence, resilient and ready to put yourself out there irrespective of your personality.
story:
Talent they say is your gateway out of poverty if you hone it. What that means is that you have to be persistence, resilient and ready to put yourself out there irrespective of your personality.
As a community builder we derive joy in bringing the best in people, this is why we want young and talented people to come showcase their talent at the second edition of the Talent Expo. Last edition of Talent Expo was impressive, exhilarating and hilarious. The dancers, singers, actors gave their best, they all came prepared. It was difficult to pick a winner and two runner up. I hope we will be thrilled this year.
As an organization who wants equal right for people, we gave our contestant daily tips on how to prepare for a talent show/competition. The first tip is to Know your Talent; this means you can be good in several things but there is one thing you enjoy doing. Take for instance you are a dancer, you can dance effortlessly, you create dance steps in your head, you enjoy dancing and you are good at it but you also have a good voice.
This means your real talent is dancing, so stick to it, improve on it, go for rehearsals and know your specialty. The second tip is to Make appropriate choice of your own unique talent i.e. honing your talent. If you are a singer, go for a song that is convenient for you. Choose the right song and the right key so you don’t bore the judges, put in the necessary practice, then get someone to listen to you and score you on a scale of 10.
Then you will know if you are making progress or not. At the end of the day the audition for the Talent Expo 2 was so amazing. 
The contestants wow the judges with their charisma, stage management and their delivery was top-notch.
The songs, poet, dance , acrobatics was exhilarating.
At the end of the day 20 contestants scale through to the final stage.
Just as the judges said "the selected contestants are not the best but the most prepared" 
Congratulations!

title: Naira Scarcity.
description: Frustration, anger linger as naira scarcity continues, as many homes and businesses are in dire straits over inability to access the new naira notes.
story:
Copied from The Nation Newspaper.
Frustration, anger linger as naira scarcity continues, as many homes and businesses are in dire straits over inability to access the new naira notes.  
Small businesses and petty traders are the worst hit as the naira paucity crisis pushes many Nigerians to the desperation mode. 
Traders of perishable food items in Nigeria are counting their losses as a result of low patronage resulting from cash scarcity. Dealers on food items such as fruits, vegetables, tomatoes, sea foods and yams are the most affected. Those who deal in perishable food items are gnashing their teeth. 
Mrs Ime Abia, who deals in fruits of all kinds at the Itam Market in Itu Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, said due to scarcity of cash, her regular customers have not been patronising her. As a result of the lack of patronage from her customers, her fruits get messed up. She complained that she can’t preserve the fruits in her refrigerator due to the epileptic power supply in the area. Mrs Abia said: “I have suffered losses. Fruits that perish easily are watermelon, cucumber, banana, pawpaw and pineapple. I spent over N30000 in purchasing these fruits because I thought I will sell them and make a good profit.
 “I don’t accept transfers. I prefer cash. So, when a few customers come, I don’t allow them to pay through transfer. How much are they even paying through transfer; N300 and N100 for banana and cucumber?”
Mallam Abdullahi Nuhu sells tomatoes, onions and pepper. He said he doesn’t accept transfers so his items are decaying. Mallam Nuhu, who was separating spoiled tomatoes and pepper from the good ones, said the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and the Federal Government should reverse the cashless policy and allow people to trade with cash.
We at Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation are urging the Federal Government of Nigeria and the CBN to end the cash and petrol crisis to ameliorate the suffering of the poor in Nigeria.

title: Elisha Foundation came to the rescue of five mothers detained at an hospital in Lagos, Nigeria.
description: UPDATE, on 5 mothers and babies that were detained by a hospital, this is to inform the public that they have been discharged on Monday 7th of November 2022...
story: In October 2022, a young guy walked into our office to solicits for help. His girlfriend that he impregnated has being detained for three months after giving birth through caesarian section (CS) in a private hospital, he was asked to pay 350,000 for the bill. He was able to pay 150,000, he needs our assistance to clear the bill. Our team at the office followed him to the hospital to talk to the admin so we can a deduction and pay the bill, but first we need to see if mother and child are okay, on getting to the ward they were kept we find out that there are 4 other women there with there child and they are held hostage too because they could not pay their bill. We had to talk to the hospital to also deduct their bills. It was not easy because the hospital refuse and our team also refused to backdown. At a point we involved the Nigerian police. UPDATE, on 5 mothers and babies that were detained by a hospital, this is to inform the public that they have been discharged on Monday 7th of November 2022, after our foundation paid the total amount 550,000 naira equivalent to 650 US DOLLAR / EUR, we are very grateful to the management of TOLU MEDICAL CENTER, for their deduction. Nigeria government has failed us. Thanks to all those who keep supporting us. Especially to Mr. Azeez who donated 10.000 naira , Mr. Christopher who donated 20,000 naira. Thanks to all ELISHA FOUNDATION team members, your fighting spirit gave us this victory. We are very much open for your donation and support, with it we can do more.

title: Praise Concert in celebration of Bro Elisha
description: The Praise Concert in celebration of Bro Elisha who is the director and founder of Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, was...
story:
The Praise Concert in celebration of Bro Elisha who is the director and founder of Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, was the first of its kind. The event held from 3:00 PM till about 06:45 PM, at Olodi-Apapa Primary school area of Omowale street, Olodi-Apapa Lagos. 
The extraordinary show of love through songs of praise and soul lifting songs of exhortation by the various guest artists to God, was like no other. Members of the communities: over 500 people came, dressed in beautiful attires, and danced to God in praise for the good deeds and love Mr. Elisha Ajose has brought to the community, through Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation. 
Fund raising in support of Elisha Development and Humanitarian foundation: which is one of the main goals of this celebration was achieved by the constant emphasis and reemphasis made by the organizers. People of different backgrounds, and organizations from both Nigeria and beyond donated sums of money to Elisha Foundation and gifts to Bro Elisha. Sums of money ranging from 1,000 Naira to 20,000 Naira. Some people who had donated in commemoration of Bro Elisha’s birthday in the past days leading to his September 6th birthday were also announced and appreciated for their kind gestures of love, faith, and belief in the works of Elisha Foundation. 
A drama by Tumise and her Crew, which featured Mr. Elisha Ajose himself, and was aimed at condemning and discouraging people against mob violence and jungle justice in the community. This drama was received by all with accolades, inspiring even the youngest and old people present.
Top dignitaries of the community, elderly and young people of repute, came out in their number to celebrate and show their love for Mr. Elisha Ajose, for the project of making lives and communities better, and changing the lives of desolate and vulnerable people in the community, all through the intervention of Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation.
Mr. Elisha Ajose had his own moment, as he cut the cake. He used this opportunity to appreciate God for his life, for the good things he’s been entrusted to do for the community. He called family members to join him in cutting the cake, and pictures were taken with individuals, members of the public, pastors and gospel ministers, who came in celebration of him. 
Mr. Elisha Ajose called all known minister of the gospel present to pray for him, and with him, and he himself rounded up the event, with soulful praise and worship. During his own personal time of praise to God, he spoke briefly about the recent event of his invitation by the Nigerian Police Authorities, the issue that led to his invitation, and his experience. He concluded by thanking God almighty for the quick and speedy resolution of the issue. Everyone joining him in praise. 
Everyone at Elisha Foundation express our deep gratitude to all artists, invited guests, donors, family members, and members of the community, who honored Mr. Elisha Ajose, and celebrated the work he is doing through Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation.  We say “Thank You” to you with strong resolution to do more for our people and our community. 
#ElishaAjoseAt46 #ElishaFoundation

title: a peaceful rally for Ajegunle
description: “Stop the Violence March”: a peaceful rally for Ajegunle, was a historical event. This rally that was organized by...
story:
“Stop the Violence March”: a peaceful rally for Ajegunle, was a historical event. This rally that was organized by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation yesterday Friday, 10th of September, 2021 was a moment for the community dwellers to face the truth and accept it. This plain and open truth that Ajegunle is insecure, and the predominant violence is the lack of firm leadership structure in the society. 
The “March” kicked off exactly 5:00 PM at Adeolu Junction area of Olodi-Apapa Lagos. Despite the dark clouds signaling imminent rainfall, and the occasional showers, volunteers of Elisha Foundation, and conscientious people of the community who aligned with the theme of the rally, came out in good number to advocate for a peaceful co-existence amongst inhabitants of the community; old and young, same and different ethnicities. 
The subject of the advocacy against violence, was made strong and resonant through the words of some volunteers and the placards of others. Pastor Semiu Lateef and Mr. Austine Tomoloju, who are very vocal volunteers of Elisha Fondation, and Mr. Elisha Ajose: founder of Elisha Foundation, gave very strong remarks to condemn violence, to challenge members of the community to be more proactive in quashing disagreement through violent means, and most importantly, a solution through the intervention of the foundation was provided.
Never has this kind of campaign done with such bold and daring strategy of calling out members who wreak havoc in the community, straight to their faces, calling them to order or risk getting punished for their crimes by prosecuting them in a court of competent jurisdiction. In same manner, solutions were proffered to same people. Solutions that would require the commitments of these mostly young people who are the bane of this society.
The messages, words, and advocacy were so intense and fierce, not watered down, even as the campaign continued until 8:30 PM at night. The “March went through Tolu Road, to Tolu Medical Center, down to New Road junction, Ojoku stree, then Ebunoti street, straight to Alhaji Salawu street, then terminating at Omowale street.
Part of the solutions provided by Mr. Elisha Ajose was the willingness of the foundation: EDHF to sponsor young people who are responsible for violent acts of the society and may be idle, who may be interested in learning trades and crafts. Mr. Elisha Ajose stated that the foundation is willing to set up those young people who would complete their crafts or trade learning, no matter the nature of it. 
Mr. Elisha Ajose in conclusion admonished the community to bond together in order to stand as a strong force against people whose interest are in stealing, maiming, raping, and violent destruction of people and the businesses in the community.  He advised members of the community to procure weapons to arm themselves against violent people, stating that self-defence is guaranteed in law. 
The rally was the talk of the town, and the good works of the foundation, received wide commendations from all and sundry. 
#ElishaFoundation #MakingLiveAndCommunitiesBetter

story:
Bro Elisha
Growing up in Olodi-Apapa area of Lagos state Nigeria with his grandmother: Mopenire Olugbeje, alongside his other siblings, aunt and uncles, Elisha Ajose, popularly known as Bro Elisha saw his fair share of how brutal and devastating poverty is.
This man: Bro Elisha did so many menial jobs, for his grandmother and for himself, in order to make ends meet and cater for his wellbeing. It was very tough and hectic, but he was consistent, making progress by progress. 
The difficulty of his condition did not limit his goal, neither did it limit his aspirations.
These menial jobs especially the one he did at the popular Boundary market for his grand uncle: Babatope Olugbeje were the beginning of his journey to greatness. At Boundary market, he collected money from commuters and market men and women who used the wooden toilet constructed on water constructed by his uncle, for convenience.
From boundary market, Bro Elisha would go to Ghana, by himself, a very young man in his late teen to early twenties. 
There was focus and discipline from all his experiences serving the Lord as a man of God, full of the spirit, teaching the divine mysteries of the kingdom of God, and his personally imbibed self discipline. 
His journey by land to Ghana and some other African countries would be the first of international experiences for him, until he reached and settled in his preferred country of Portugal with his beautiful family.
Bro Elisha Ajose speaks Yoruba, English, Hausa, Igbo, Portuguese and Polish fluently. Although, he didn't get to finish his secondary education in Nigeria, he, in the course of his journey, learnt by books, by studying, and eventually sponsoring himself for university education in Europe.
Bro Elisha is a man worth celebrating. He is a worthy role model in a moral and vision deficient place from whence he hailed.
He has inspired hundreds of people to give selflessly and serve voluntarily, through Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation. He has lifted families and non-families to a place of honour and self sufficiently.
Through Elisha Foundation, he's given hope and love back to a community that offered him little. He is a rare gem that we celebrate today, for his selfless relentless love, his undying spirit for change, and his inestimable investments in and for a lot of people. 
Thank you so much for your sacrifice, love, and care sir.
Bro Elisha has requested that the appreciation and celebrating he wants to be honoured with, by anyone who cares to honour him, should not be in physical gifts or beautifully crafted words, but in donation of money and material resources to Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, in order to help him and his team do more.
We love you so much sir. 
Happy birthday to you!

description: Today's Free Medical outreach, organised by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, in partnership with OlaLion Pharmaceuticals was...
story:
Today's Free Medical outreach, organised by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, in partnership with OlaLion Pharmaceuticals was a profound moment that reemphasized the importance of good public health policy in our community.
Members of the public thronged out in huge numbers at around Past 6:00 AM, for a program that should begin at 8:00 AM.
Quickly the venue was set up, the children deworming section away form the adults blood test, blood pressure and Body mass index test area. 
Mr. Olasimbo Anjorin : the CEO of OlaLion Pharmaceuticals addressed the crowd on the significance of each test, and the importance of good health for each individual and the community collectively.
The programme soon began as each volunteer nurse of Elisha Foundation and others nurses from OlaLion Pharmaceuticals handled different tests desks and drugs prescription desks in a very efficient and organised way. 
Volunteers of Elisha Foundation, in their numbers helped in taking height readings, weight readings, body mass index tests, coordination of children, adults, numbering and record taking.
Everyone present was each occupied in valuable acts of service for the community, as it pertains to peoples' health.
The biggest part of the work and the part that required the highest amount of time, medical attention, and volume of people, was the optometrist section, where children and adult eye tests were conducted. Reading glasses were provided for 40 people and quality prescription for those who couldn't get glasses.
Free medicines and medical supplies were given out to everyone who required it, according to the diagnosis and results for the tests carried out.
The optometry: eye session was well packed out. It was a reminded that eye related health challenge is a major and rampant challenge being faced by people of different age groups. The eye is an important part of the body. It is to be taken very good care.
We encourage and challenge the Local government:Ajeromi-Ifelodun Local Government, the Lagos State Government, and the Nigerian government to prioritize public health, revitalize our public institutions to restore public confidence in our public institutions.
Health is wealth. Good and quality health is the most fundamental human right.
We appreciate Mr. Olasimbo Anjorin and all our volunteers for the rigorous work of creating a sustainable and healthy society.
Thank you.
#ElishaFoundation

title: A NEW BILL STOPPING THE ARREST OF PERSONS RESIDING IN LAGOS STATE
description: LAGOS STATE HOUSE OF ASSEMBLY, ON MONDAY, 16TH AUGUST, 2021, PASSED A NEW BILL STOPPING THE ARREST OF...
story:
LAGOS STATE HOUSE OF ASSEMBLY, ON MONDAY, 16TH AUGUST, 2021, PASSED A NEW BILL STOPPING THE ARREST OF PERSONS RESIDING IN LAGOS STATE, WITHOUT AN ARREST WARRANT.
Here are five major things all Lagos residents and visitors should know about the new law:
1. No more parading of suspect by police
Unlike the case of Chidinma Ojukwu and other suspects in the past, police will no more parade a suspect before the media as the amended version of the Criminal Justice Law of the state has put a stop to the act.
“As from the commencement of this law, the police shall refrain from parading any suspect before the media.” The law states.
2. Arrest without warrant
The new law makes it mandatory for police to present an arrest warrant before arresting a suspect, and the only condition to do otherwise is when the person is reasonably suspected to unlawfully be in possession of firearms or other such dangerous instruments.
In any case where the suspect does not possess weapons or firearms unlawfully, the police must show a warrant of arrest.
3.No more arrest in lieu 
This means that a family member or relations of a suspect can no longer be arrested and only the alleged suspect may be arrested.
The Nigerian Police are used to arresting every person they meet at an arrest location whether the suspect is there or not, this act is no more legal and the police in Lagos can now be sued for arrested friends or family members of a suspect.
4. No more harassments or torture
The new law bars the police from harassing or torturing a suspect before or after arrest.
"A suspect should also be accorded humane treatment, with the right to dignity of person; not subjected to any form of torture, cruel, inhumane or degrading treatment; be brought before the court as prescribed by this law or any other written law; or be released conditionally or unconditionally.” The law states.
5. Access to lawyer:
The new law stipulates that a suspect has the right to a lawyer and must not be held in custody beyond the lawful day.
"A person arrested shall be given reasonable facilities for obtaining legal advice, bail or making arrangements for defense or release.” States the new bill.

title: United Ajax Soccer Academy vs AJ Chelsea Football Club
description: The final match: United Ajax Soccer Academy vs AJ Chelsea Football Club had been widely anticipated. This match which followed...
story:
The final match: United Ajax Soccer Academy vs AJ Chelsea Football Club had been widely anticipated. This match which followed the grand style closing ceremony, commenced also with great finesse. Both teams matched to the field in custom jerseys made and designed in the logo of Elisha Foundation. The Nigerian Anthem was sung by all present in an unusual way, as the C&S Ifelodun, J.M.J. Quarters Army of Salvation led the spectators and teams with their beats from the drum, leading the anthem. 
The commentator was a man of many words and sound knowledge of history. He guided the spectators and online partakers with clear commentaries that put a live to the game. The game in the midst of these commentaries gave a sensation of a world class football tournament, hosted by top professionals and organizations of football. 
The game started at 04:15 PM, after the elaborate grand closing ceremony. The game, expected to be with very intense competition, with attacks and counter-attacks like have never been seen before in this tournament. So, it was just exactly. AJ Chelsea F.C. hit the ground running with very fierce attacks that may lead one to believe that this match is a sure win for them. United Ajax did not lag behind, strongly repelling their strong force, with a force that match it. 11 minutes after the match began, AJ Chelsea successfully scored a goal that got their whole fan base hailing and happy. Efe Samuel (15) scored this resounding goal and the team jubilated uncontrollably. This goal certainly sent determination and resolution for a ‘clear tug-of-war’ in this match.  
The goal by AJ Chelsea was certainly not acceptable by United Ajax team as the e final goal of this match. Certainly not in this final game! This giant stride determination for winning was displayed at 04:36 PM by Bayo (03) of United Ajax with his equalizing goal that leveled the playing field between both teams. What more could be expected from a final match, except a fiercely competed game such as this.  The 1st half ended at 04:45, and all teams went for a reinforcement, in words from their coaches, to gear each team for more actions, in the latter part of this game. 
During the half-time, JaftJay dance company did a remarkable dance and choreography for the spectators and everyone present enjoyed the performance. This obvious appreciation could be seen from the cheers and applause this crew got during and after their very rousing performance. 
Sunny Idoko Enalegwu: the man with the golden voice, and the 2nd place winner Talent Expo 2021, gave this half-time a moment of lyrical fun and entertainment with his renowned performance that swept spectators of their feets. This performance rounded the half-time special.
The 2nd half began at 05:00 PM. Goals anticipated by fans, players, and indeed coaches on both sides of the divide. Goal attempts were made by both teams and each of these goal attempts was foiled by a very strong defense or was incomplete. Much of this part of the game were attacks and counter-attacks, none of which delivered any goal to both teams. 
The 2nd half ended at 05:32 PM with 1-1 goal on both sides. The penalties quickly came in as both teams slug it out with one another. A clear winner had to emerge. 
With Tosin (01) of AJ Chelsea at the goalpost, United Ajax players needed to be weary of their shots. Tosin is rumored as a very excellent goal-keeper, with very sharp instincts of going for the ball. Indeed, the rumors were true. Tosin (01) of AJ Chelsea F.C. defended his team and gave them a renowned victory in penalty shoot-out. The penalty which ended 3 - 4, with AJ Chelsea F.C. winning, and catapulting itself as the 1st place winner of the Ajegunle Under-19 football competition. 
AJ Chelsea won, their jubilation and excitements filled the whole arena. The massive show of affections was a moment to see and appreciate. It was indeed beautiful beyond words. There is a joy that comes with winning. 
The referees, 3rd, 2nd, and 1st place teams were given a medal of excellent performance through out this tournament. 
Trophies were awarded to each of these 3 winning teams, and the cash prizes as follows:
1st Place: 500,000 Naira
2nd Place: 300,000 Naira
3rd Place: 200,000 Naira
Commendation prizes of 50,000 Naira were awarded to the following teams and players, in the categories listed below:
Best behaved Team: Klassisch Football Academy
Best Coach: Kehinde Ogundoghone of Young Star Football Club
Highest Goal Scorer: Joseph Aderibole of Young Star Football Club
Most Valuable Player: Lajuwomi Moses Adeyemi of Young Star Football Club
Best Keeper: Tosin Emoruwa of AJ Chelsea Football Club
With this these prizes announced, wounded up the final match of the Ajegunle Under-19 Football Tournament 2021, host: Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation.

story:
The football gallery and the immediate surrounding of the field at the Nigerian Navy barracks, Mobil Road, Apapa, were packed out with fans and football lovers, in the penultimate game of this Ajegunle Under-19 football tournament, hosted by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation. 
This widely anticipated match between Young Star F.C. and Christ Ambassador Sporting Academy was certain to be a very competitive game, whose result would be highly devastating on one and very rewarding for the other team. It is a game to compete for the 3rd place position in this well circulated and popular Ajegunle Under-19 football tournament. 
The match kicked off at 04:06 PM, and soon became as competitive as was anticipated by all. Young Star F.C. was quick to be combative, attacking on all fronts. Christ Ambassador F.C. didn’t lag also in its defense and attacks too. This combativeness led Juwon (21) of Young Star F.C. to give his team a resounding goal at 04:27 PM. The first half ended shortly after at 04:38 PM.
During the half time, the Secretary of Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation: Sanni Sunday Emmanuel addressed the Spectators about the goal and objective of this tournament, and also briefly discussed the charitable works of Elisha Development and Humanitarian foundation. He then introduced to the spectators one of the Aid-workers at Elisha Foundation: Miss Titilope Olumofin, who spoke on a very important subject of Suicide. She explained the effects of suicide, its prevalence in our society, how to prevent it, and how to seek for help if one became suicidal. This brief explanation and education on this subject received wide attention and was highly received by the sport loving spectators who were eager to see the second half of the contested game. 
After this educative piece by Miss Titlope Olumofin on suicide, Sunny Idoko Enalegwu who was the 2nd place winner of Talent Expo, organized by Elisha Foundation in March 2021, was received by the spectators, as he delivered in his usual manner a very lovely and arousing rendition of “Stand up for the Champion” song. His delivery was superb and his golden voice created a moment of true appreciation for the art of music by the football loving spectators. His performance earned him a great many applauses and shouts by the spectators there gathered. 
Soon after that was the surprise cake and celebration of Mr. James Adesuyi, a very valued member and stack holder at Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundaion. He was introduced by Sanni Sunday Emmanuel. A bit of his impacts spoken about, the volunteers of Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation gathered around him to celebrate him. The spectators stood up in celebration for Mr. James Adesuyi as he celebrated his birthday.
The 2nd half began 04:52PM. Each team with more resolution than the first part of the game. Would Christ Ambassador allow themselves to be beaten a second time at a field considered home to them? The match so far seemed that may just be so. Christ Ambassador were certainly not about to allow this ongoing defeat to stand. Their counter attacks were equally intense, more so than the first part of the game. Young Star F.C. is also determined to leave this game victorious by a good margin it would seem. 
Juwon (21) of Young Star F.C. at 04:54PM gave his team a headway by scoring another goal that seemed to bring the dream of Young Star F.C. closer to realization. Joy filled the whole fan base of Young Star F.C. with very visible excitements and anticipation for a quick end to the game, signaling an obvious victory for Young Star F.C.
This joy on the faces of the fans and indeed the players of Young Star F.C. soon began to fade when Timi (05) 3 minutes after Juwon’s latter goal, at 04:57 PM gave his team: Christ Ambassador a beautiful goal which led to a quick disruption and unsettling in the Young Star F.C. camp.
The game continued with fans clearly either expressing hope and excitement either for the game to end, or for a goal to be scored, depending on which team or fan you ask.  The odds seemed a bit against Young Star F.C. as this lone goal scored by Christ Ambassador F.C. seemed to have heightened their hope, and increased their commitments, attacks, force, and defense against Young Star F.C. This decisiveness and coordinated agility towards a goal by Christ Ambassador F.C. soon paid off about 5 minutes to the end of the 2nd half, when at 05:16 PM Azeez (16) of Christ Ambassador scored an equalizing and last goal of this game against Young Star F.C.
This brings the game to a draw, leading to a penalty shoot-out between both teams. The penalty was equally as competitively contested as the game, and ended with 7 goals to 8, as Christ Ambassador emerged 3rd place in the Ajegunle Under-19 football tournament, hosted by Elisha development and Humanitarian Foundation. 
Anticipation of the final match is in earnest between United Ajax Soccer Academy, and AJ Chelsea F.C., later today, with closing ceremony beginning by 03:00PM and Kick-off at 04:00 PM.

story:
To our dear Mr.  Adesuyi James
In life's journey, we all crave true love. We want to be loved unconditionally. We want to be around people who genuinely love us, and can make sacrifices for us. People we can be vulnerable around, knowing that we won't be taken advantage of.
At Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, we found in Mr. James Adesuyi, such a man and companion. A leader that is always ready to serve with all sense of selflessness, humility, and humanity.
At Elisha Foundation, we get to meet, help, discuss with, encourage, and strengthen vulnerable, weak, hopeless, and sick people.
In order to be able to help these people in  need, in order to know their true challenge so that they may be helped at their very point of need, they must first trust us to be a reliable confidant they can talk to.
Mr. James Adesuyi has in the past one year since the establishment of Elisha Foundation, being a solid rock upon which people find trust and strength in the foundation. He's been able to get our team of volunteers to work together, and produce  maximum impacts intended in the lives of people in our community.
All of us from Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, wish Mr. James Adesuyi a very happy birthday. We truly love and appreciate your dedication, love, and leadership you've provided so far.
Thank you sir!
Happy birthday sir!

The match: Christ Ambassador Sporting Academy vs AJ Chelsea F.C. was a game that could be tagged ‘survival of the fittest’ by football pundits. Christ Ambassador in their usual blue met AJ Chelsea in their pure white. It seemed a game that holds so much excitement and thrill for football lovers. 
Christ Ambassador had been unbeaten since the tournament began. The football field which is home to Christ Ambassador, being their training arena has very well been defended by them in all their previous matches. Christ Ambassador had in their first match against Na God Pro F.C. beaten them in game 2 goals to none and 7 goals to 1 against Joe Football Academy. 
The football skill by AJ Chelsea which was widely commented upon as was expected by their fan base, was widely spoken of amongst the spectators. Their Goal-keeper Tosin Emokuwa (01) was widely spoken of as very skilled and dynamic. 
The match kicked off in earnest by 04:02 PM and much of the match were attacks and counter attacks by both sides of the teams. The first half ended by 04:32 PM without goals by both sides of the game.
During the half time, Sunday Gabriel Sewanu a.k.a. Lala performed two songs for the spectators. Lala’s presentation received a resounding applause after his rhythm filled lyrical song and rap. Sunday won the first prize in Talent Expo, a talent exposition event for talented artists of Ajegunle, which was hosted by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, in March 2021.
The 2nd half commenced by 04:45 PM, and like the first half, many attacks and counter attacks. It would seem like this game would end without any goal on both sides, like the previous semifinal match played yesterday. The 2nd half ended by 05:15 PM with no goal from both teams. This brings the 2 semifinal matches of this tournament to matches without any goal recorded. 
This led to penalty shoots. This penalty shoots quickly finished as Tosin Emokuwa (01), the goalkeeper of AJ Chelsea F.C. showed himself as indeed skilled beyond mere words. He conceded no goal in penalty shoot-out, by all 3 players of Christ Ambassador Sporting Academy. 
This brings the match to an end, with AJ Chelsea proceeding to the final match against United Ajax Sporting Academy, while Christ Ambassador tussle it out with Young Star F.C. for the 3rd place.

title: Suicide is a mental health problem
description: One can be mentally unwell, just as one can be physically unwell. Mental health is as important as physical health.
story:
What is mental health? 
Mental health, defined by the World Health Organization, is "a state of well-being in which the individual realizes his or her own abilities, can cope with the normal stresses of life, can work productively and fruitfully, and is able to make a contribution to his or her community"
One can be mentally unwell, just as one can be physically unwell. Mental health is as important as physical health. 
In low to middle income countries, mental health is usually a stigma, and receives very little to no attention from People, and government. Mental health problems such as suicide are particularly rampant. WHO reports put it at “79% of global suicides occur in low- and middle-income countries”.
Close to 800 000 people die due to suicide every year, and Suicide is the third leading cause of death in 15-19-year-olds.
Why are young people the most affected demography of suicide, and why are low to middle income countries the most represented in this unhealthy statistic?
It is because low to middle income countries have a barrage of societal problems that could potentially result into depression and ultimately suicide. Such societal problems as: abuse, underemployment, lack of employment, discrimination, etc. 
These aforementioned issues are a fundamental problem in most low-middle income countries, which affect the quality of lives of people, especially young people living therein. Since the problems are usually community or country based, they usually take a mental toll and cause severe mental stress to young people who are just growing up, desiring to live their best but being constantly weighed down by impossibilities of the societies.
The constant thinking and stressing to improve one’s standard of living without much progress, due to reasons beyond one’s control could lead to substance abuse and excessive drinking of alcohol. Substance abuse such as usage of drugs, and excessive alcohol can create euphoria for some young people, and drive some into deep depression, causing them to always stay alone, or think deeply about the essence of life in general. This cause them to question the relevance of their own existence.
It is estimated according to WHO that around 20% of global suicides are due to pesticide self-poisoning, most of which occur in rural agricultural areas in low- and middle-income countries. The use of pesticides and other crude means to take one’s life is borne out of the fact that these are the most basic tools available for people within the low-middle income countries. 
Suicide is a problem that affect families and communities’ alike. It creates a void and an atmosphere of helplessness. It portrays a society as bleak and void of hope, especially for young people. Predominant suicides within a community is a symbol of poor quality of lives of people within a particular community.
HOW TO PREVENT SUICIDE
Suicide is a serious public health problem; however, suicides are preventable with timely, evidence-based and often low-cost interventions. For national responses to be effective, a comprehensive multisectoral suicide prevention strategy is needed.
PREVENTION AND CONTROL
Suicides are preventable. There are a number of measures that can be taken at population, sub-population and individual levels to prevent suicide and suicide attempts. These include:
- reducing access to the means of suicide (e.g., pesticides, firearms, certain medications);
- reporting by media in a responsible way;
- school-based interventions;
- introducing alcohol policies to reduce the harmful use of alcohol; early identification, treatment and care of people with mental and substance use disorders, chronic pain and acute emotional distress;
- training of non-specialized health workers in the assessment and management of suicidal behavior;
- follow-up care for people who attempted suicide and provision of community support.
As a Foundation that care about the wellbeing of people, we condemn suicide and we want the idea it to be perished. Suicide is not the solution towards any life problem or challenges. Such as financial problems, relationship break-ups, chronic pain, illness, conflict, disaster, violence, abuse, or loss and isolation. 
Remember, you are stronger than all of these. If you need someone to talk to, we are here for you. We shall overcome. 
SAY NO TO SUICIDE!
Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation

title: International Workers’ Day
description: International Workers’ Day is a celebration of working  people and  a day  when people campaign for  decent work  and  fair  pay...
story:
International Workers’ Day is a celebration of working  people and  a day  when people campaign for  decent work  and  fair  pay.  Thanks  to  action taken by  workers  over  many  years, millions  of people have  won fundamental  rights  and  protections.  Minimum  wages  have  been established,  there  are limits  on working  hours,  and  people  have the right  to  paid  holidays  and sick  pay.   
However,  in recent  years,  working  conditions  in many  situations  have  got worse.  Since  the global financial crisis  of  2008,  part-time,  short-term  and badly  paid work  has  become  more common,  and  state  pensions  are  at risk.  We have  also  seen the rise  of the  ‘gig economy’, where companies  hire workers  casually  for  one short  job  at a  time.  These workers  don’t have the usual  rights  to  paid  holidays,  the  minimum  wage or  redundancy  pay.  Solidarity  with other workers  is  as  important as  ever. 
The history  of  International  Workers’  Day In May 1886,  400,000  workers  in many  parts  of  the  USA went on strike,  demanding  an eighthour  working  day.  The strike started  peacefully,  but on the  third  day  of protests  in  Chicago there was  some violence.  The police shot at unarmed  workers,  killing  several  of them.  The next  day  there were more protests  and  someone  threw  a bomb.  Seven police officers  and four  workers  were  killed  by  the bomb  or  police shooting  just  after  the bomb.  The person who threw  the bomb  was  never  identified,  but  eight workers  were arrested.  Seven of them  were sentenced  to  death,  and  one of  them  was  sent  to  prison  for  15  years.   This  event,  known as  The Haymarket  Affair,  was  very  important in bringing  working  people together  in  the  USA.  Many  people  didn’t believe the men were guilty,  and  the  trial  was criticised  for  being  unfair.  The Haymarket  Affair  became  an international  symbol  of the struggle for  workers’  rights,  and  May  1  was  chosen  to  be International  Workers’  Day.  On this day,  socialist parties  and  trade unions  called  for  workers  to  demonstrate  for  the eight-hour day  and  in favour  of peaceful  protest.  The eight-hour  working  day  became law  for  public workers  in 1892  in the USA.  Since then,  workers’  movements  all  over  the  world  have continued  to  fight for  and  win  this  right.     How  is  Workers’  Day  celebrated  now? Celebrations  and  protests  take place  in different ways  in different countries  around  the world. May  1  is  a public  holiday  in countries  such  as Nigeria, South Africa,  Tunisia,  Tanzania,  Zimbabwe and China.  In  many  countries,  including  France,  Greece,  Japan,  Pakistan,  the  United  Kingdom  and the United  States,  there  are demonstrations  on  International  Workers’  Day.   Workers’  Day  is  a day  for  working  people to  have  a rest from  their  usual  labour.  It is  an opportunity  to  campaign for  workers’  rights,  show  solidarity  with other  working  people and  to celebrate the achievements  of workers  all  over  the world. 
So we advocate for better salary, better working condition. We say no to child labour. We say Happy Workers' Day to all workers. May the Lord bless your labour and make you eat the fruits of your labour.

These workers  don’t have the usual  rights  to  paid  holidays,  the  minimum  wage or  redundancy  pay.  Solidarity  with other workers  is  as  important as  ever. 
The history  of  International  Workers’  Day In May 1886,  400,000  workers  in many  parts  of  the  USA went on strike,  demanding  an eighthour  working  day.  The strike started  peacefully,  but on the  third  day  of protests  in  Chicago there was  some violence.  The police shot at unarmed  workers,  killing  several  of them.  The next  day  there were more protests  and  someone  threw  a bomb.  Seven police officers  and four  workers  were  killed  by  the bomb  or  police shooting  just  after  the bomb.  The person who threw  the bomb  was  never  identified,  but  eight workers  were arrested.  Seven of them  were sentenced  to  death,  and  one of  them  was  sent  to  prison  for  15  years.   This  event,  known as  The Haymarket  Affair,  was  very  important in bringing  working  people together  in  the  USA.  Many  people  didn’t believe the men were guilty,  and  the  trial  was criticised  for  being  unfair.  The Haymarket  Affair  became  an international  symbol  of the struggle for  workers’  rights,  and  May  1  was  chosen  to  be International  Workers’  Day.  On this day,  socialist parties  and  trade unions  called  for  workers  to  demonstrate  for  the eight-hour day  and  in favour  of peaceful  protest.  The eight-hour  working  day  became law  for  public workers  in 1892  in the USA.  Since then,  workers’  movements  all  over  the  world  have continued  to  fight for  and  win  this  right.     How  is  Workers’  Day  celebrated  now? Celebrations  and  protests  take place  in different ways  in different countries  around  the world. May  1  is  a public  holiday  in countries  such  as Nigeria, South Africa,  Tunisia,  Tanzania,  Zimbabwe and China.  In  many  countries,  including  France,  Greece,  Japan,  Pakistan,  the  United  Kingdom  and the United  States,  there  are demonstrations  on  International  Workers’  Day.   Workers’  Day  is  a day  for  working  people to  have  a rest from  their  usual  labour.  It is  an opportunity  to  campaign for  workers’  rights,  show  solidarity  with other  working  people and  to celebrate the achievements  of workers  all  over  the world. 
So we advocate for better salary, better working condition. We say no to child labour. We say Happy Workers' Day to all workers. May the Lord bless your labour and make you eat the fruits of your labour.

story:
The much anticipated grand finale of Ajegunle Spelling Bee on Saturday the 24th of April 26, 2021 organized by Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation was a remarkable day of expectation and excitements for all 39 finalists. Suspense filled atmosphere, as contestants, their parents and guardians, members of the audience keenly spectated with glee.
The Spelling Bee kicked off with the MC: Mr. Seun Akinyemi who introduced the program to the public and ushered to the stage Mr. Semiu Lateef: a clergy man, and a volunteer with Elisha Foundation, who led the opening prayer. This was immediately followed by the national anthem of Nigeria. 
The opening address was given by Sanni Sunday Emmanuel, the secretary of Elisha Foundation. The opening address clarified the goal, the prizes for the winners, and the programs the Foundation has for all 39 finalist. 4 winners were expected to emerge from each of the category, and each winner wins a 250,000 naira academic scholarship grant. 
A song with educative lyrical content was performed by the 1st and 2nd place winner of the Talent Expo: Sunday Gabriel Sewanu and Sunny Idoko Enalegwu respectively. Their performances were followed by a short drama presentation on the gains of education, by the 3rd place winner of the Talent Expo: Kolawole Tunmise. 
Rounding off this session was a beautiful dance rendition, and explanation of the beautiful words of the Nigerian anthem by Peace dance crew. Miss Vivian delivered a rousing spoken word, and Azuka, a visually impaired DJ showed his skill to the whole world. 
The competition kicked off earnestly for all four categories and four winners soon emerged. 
1. Name: Adenekan Aliyat; Class: School Basic 3;
School: 1st D'eko International .
2. Name: Badmus .R.Adunni; Class: Basic 4;
School: Omo Nursery and Primary School.
3. Name: Wasiu Afeez Olanrewaju; Class: JSS     1;
School: Realistic Goals Secondary School.
4. Name: Akpan Blessing Edidiong; Class: SSS    3; 
School: Bola Ige  Millennium Senior Secondary School.
The judges who presided over the spelling events were:
1. Mr. Tomoloju Austine Olamide
2. Miss Gbemi Ogunkalu
3. Mr. Gbenga Apeyiomo
The founder of Elisha Foundation: Mr. Elisha Ajose, came on stage to educate the public on what inspired the Spelling Bee Competition. He admonished members of the public to continue to encourage their children for scholarly and academic improvements. 
The 39 finalists were given certificates of participation, and a bag pack with a dictionary, pens, and pencils. 
The competition was closed with the national anthem, sang by Sunny Idoko Enalegwu 2nd place winner of the Talent Expo.

title: WE STAND AGAINST CHILD HAWKER.
description: Hawking by children is a form of child labour and it contravenes the Child Rights Act which stipulates that children under the...
story: Hawking by children is a form of child labour and it contravenes the Child Rights Act which stipulates that children under the age of 18 should not engage in any work that is mentally, physically, socially or morally dangerous and harmful to them, preventing them from going to school; obliging them to leave school prematurely or to combine school attendance with excessively long or heavy work. According to International Labour Organization, the number of working children under the age of 14 in Nigeria is estimated at 15million. Research has it, that street hawking by children constitutes one of the major forms of child labour, by implication a larger percentage of these children are on the street. This trend is quite disturbing, especially with the number increasing daily. In many cities across the country, it is not uncommon to see little children, ranging from age 9 to13, hawking various goods on the roads. Some even take up the hazardous task of bus conductors. These children, who hawk by the roadsides, usually suffer from fatigue, irregular attendance at school, if enrolled at all, lack of comprehension and motivation, improper socialisation, exposure to the risk of sexual abuse, high likelihood of being involved in crime. Many have argued that severe economic pressure is responsible for this heinous practice. But then, when placed side by side the inherent dangers associated with child hawking, engaging children in such highly volatile practice, under whatever disguise, should be condemned and discouraged by all and sundry.

story: Community development is "a process where community members come together to take collective action and generate solutions to common problems." It is a broad concept, applied to the practices of civic leaders, activists, involved citizens, and professionals to improve various aspects of communities, typically aiming to build stronger and more resilient local communities.  Community development is also understood as a professional discipline, and is defined by the International Association for Community Development as "a practice-based profession and an academic discipline that promotes participative democracy, sustainable development, rights, economic opportunity, equality and social justice, through the organisation, education and empowerment of people within their communities, whether these be of locality, identity or interest, in urban and rural settings". Community development seeks to empower individuals and groups of people with the  skills they need to effect change within their communities. These skills are often created through the formation of social groups working for a common agenda.  Community developers must understand both how to work with individuals and how  to affect communities' positions within the context of larger social institutions.

description: Independence Day Nigeria (1 October 1960) is an official national holiday in Nigeria, celebrated on the first of October. It marks...
story: Independence Day Nigeria (1 October 1960) is an official national holiday in Nigeria, celebrated on the first of October. It marks Nigeria's proclamation of independence from British rule on 1 October 1960. So for this reason, Nigeria celebrates its independence on 1 October every year. The festivities begin with the President's address to the people, which is broadcast on radio and television. In 1914, the Southern Nigeria Protectorate was combined with the Northern Nigeria Protectorate to create the Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria, which has the borders of modern-day Nigeria. By the late 1950s, the call for independence of territories in Africa and the decline of the British Empire led to the country being granted independence on 1 October 1960 as the Federation of Nigeria. Three years later, the constitution was amended and the country was declared the Federal Republic of Nigeria with Nnamdi Azikiwe, previously Governor-General, as the first President. We feel reluctant in wishing Nigeria as a nation Happy Independence Day, however our glorious wishes go to all Nigerians, Happy Independence, freedom from bad government, freedom from poverty, sickness and pain. May this day brings you liberty that you seek for.

title: WE CELEBRATE OUR FOUNDER AND CHAIRMAN
description: IT'S A GREAT DAY! WE CELEBRATE OUR FOUNDER AND CHAIRMAN...
story: IT'S A GREAT DAY! WE CELEBRATE OUR FOUNDER AND CHAIRMAN. Bro Elisha Today, we celebrate a great man. A man with a huge heart, a caring father, an entrepreneurial person, and a truly selfless leader. Mr. Elisha Ajose is many things to different people. He is a man that can truly be regarded as a leader.  "Without Charity, we are nothing". This is his favourite quote, and no person exemplifies these words like Bro Elisha. He personifies the message of these words in ways that confounds all reasoning and understanding.  Ajegunle doesn't have a lot of role models for the teaming young population. Elisha Ajose is more than a role model, more than a mentor, and more than a benefactor to ask for. A lot of people grew from Ajegunle to become rich and wealthy, but as they grew, they grew further away and distant. Elisha Ajose grew closer and more closely knitted with the poor, the malnourished, and the vulnerable. He is that little glow of hope in thick and hopeless darkness.  Elisha Ajose is a gem to behold! Join us to celebrate a man of many children and many parents. He is a father figure to far too many people, and a son of consolations, to many elderly people, who have spent their days, in the scary hallow Chambers of torture, of the Nigerian state.  His foundation: Elisha Development and Humanitarian Foundation, has been a beaming icon to hopeless people, both within and outside Ajegunle. Words are not enough to communicate our gratitude and immense Thanks to the service, love, and gladness Elisha Ajose has shared with a community that contributed little to nothing in his life. The hope and opportunities he never had, he now offers to many, through E.D.H.F. Everything that we have achieved so far in our 5 months of existence, has been possible, because you gave yourself to put a smile on many faces. Though you know it won't be easy, but with determination and strength made possible by love and dedication, you keep pressing on.  Who would have thought that AJ City could in today's nigeria where only money motivates, would have youths that are inspired to volunteer without expecting any material benefit in return.  Where people expected businesses and establishments for profits, you gave shelters and food, without expecting profits.  Where people expected a loan, you gave financial aids, and support, to bring people out of misery and agony.  All of us volunteers at E.D.H.F., say 'Thank you to you'.  We love you sir! Happy birthday to you!

story: The real age of consent in Nigeria is 18. Section 31 (3) (a) of the Child's Rights Act 2003 states that, “Where a person is charged with an offence (of unlawful sexual relations with a child) under this section (31 of the same act), it is immaterial that the offender believed the person to be of or above the age of eighteen years.”  A person who commits an act which causes penetration with a child is guilty of an offence called defilement. A person who commits an offence of defilement with a child aged eleven years or less shall upon conviction be sentenced to imprisonment for life. A person who commits an offence of defilement with a child between the age of twelve and fifteen years is liable upon conviction to imprisonment for life. A person who commits an offence of defilement with a child between the age of sixteen and eighteen years is liable upon conviction to imprisonment for life.

Section 31 (3) (a) of the Child's Rights Act 2003 states that, “Where a person is charged with an offence (of unlawful sexual relations with a child) under this section (31 of the same act), it is immaterial that the offender believed the person to be of or above the age of eighteen years.”  A person who commits an act which causes penetration with a child is guilty of an offence called defilement. A person who commits an offence of defilement with a child aged eleven years or less shall upon conviction be sentenced to imprisonment for life. A person who commits an offence of defilement with a child between the age of twelve and fifteen years is liable upon conviction to imprisonment for life. A person who commits an offence of defilement with a child between the age of sixteen and eighteen years is liable upon conviction to imprisonment for life.

title: illegal tenancy agreement fees and unlawful agent fees
description: We are calling on all landlords, caretakers and agent to put an end to illegal tenancy agreement fees and unlawful agent fees...
story: We are calling on all landlords, caretakers and agent to put an end to illegal tenancy agreement fees and unlawful agent fees. Legally the tenancy agreement fees is a fee paid to a lawyer for drafting  a rental contract between the landlord and the tenant. Infact the agreement fees is called LEGAL FEES. Which is supposed to be 5% of the tenancy rates.For instance, if the property is going for N60,000 per annum,the agreement fee will be 5% of N60,000 which amounts to N3,000 for one year and if the landlord is collecting 2 years rent, that’s N3,000 x 2 years which is N6,000.Note it is illegal to force 2 years rent on a tenant. Many landlord do not give a written contract not to mention involving a lawyer, which makes the agreement fees illegal, no landlord or caretaker should demand for any agreement fees without a written agreement by a lawyer.  Lawful agent fees should be 10% of the tenancy rates.For instance, if the property is going for N60,000 per annum, the agency fee will be 10% of N60,000 which amounts to N6,000 for one year and if is 2 years rent, that’s N6,000 x 2 years which is N12,000. So any agent fees beyond 10% is unlawful charges.  We are calling on agents, caretakers and landlords to please stop this atrocities that have been going on for too long. How can we fight the government for predicament of the citizens are inflicting pain upon one another. How can you tell someone renting a room of N4,000 per month,N48,000 annual to pay agreement fees of N50,000 and agent fees of N50,000. This is inhumane. We therefore call on all citizens to stand up against this atrocities. By writing complaint letter to every Local Government, State House of Assembly, National Assembly and Federal Ministry of Land,Housing and Urban Development.  By making a peaceful protest in front of every Local Government, State House of Assembly,National Assembly and Federal Ministry of Land,Housing and Urban development. We are the people to make Nigeria a better place.

story: Children's Day is a commemorative date celebrated annually in honor of children, whose date of observance varies by country. In 1925, International Children's Day was first proclaimed in Geneva during the World Conference on Child Welfare. Since then, it is celebrated on June 1 in most countries. Children's Day is celebrated by the UN on November 20. In Nigeria it is celebrated May 27. We wish all the children in Nigeria  Happy Children's Day, and we say NO to child abuse, NO to child trafficking, NO to child negligent. YES education and better life for all children.

story: Cleanliness they say is next to godliness. Elisha Development Humanitarian Foundation has decided to come up with a competition where all streets can participate in cleaning their streets and 10 cleanest streets get a give away prize. The Winners will be announced by 8th of June 2020.  We found out that if each street is clean, there will be reduction in illness and disease and our environment will be clean. Let's keep our community clean. HOW TO PARTICIPATE Get as much people in your street to sweep, clean the gutters, drainage, and dump the trashes at the entrance of each street where LAWMA can easily pack it. Take a picture of the street before and after the cleanup and send it to our Facebook page. You should also upload on your personal Facebook page, then tag our page. Don't forget to use the hashtag #CleanYourStreetChallenge. We will pick the cleanest street . HOW WINNERS WOULD BE SELECTED 10 winners would be picked!  The #CleanYourStreetChallenge begins on Monday the 18th of May, and Ends on Monday the 1st of June, 2020. Multiples pictures of different cleaning exercise  on the same street is allowed, and that increases the chances of winning. NOTE: Pictures of Before and After the cleaning has been done can be uploaded on your various social media pages, and then tagging us. No picture sent or uploaded after 1st of June would be accepted or consisdered. Be Clean... Live Healthy!  #CleanYourStreetChallenge

story: Leadership they say, is simply making the system better than you have met it. We did it! On Saturday, the 4th of April, 2020, we provide to over 320 families, who are most needy and vulnerable among us with food packages which consisted: 1. Rice of 5kg and 10kg 2. 5kg of Beans 3. Half carton (20 pieces of 70g) Noodles We estimated that this is representative of over 2,000 families, in the slum of Olodi-Apapa, Ajegunle, Lagos Nigeria. We are glad to have provided hope, and showed love to people who truly need help during this crisis, regardless of their tribes or ethnicity. More than 150 families have since reached out to us since then, for support. We want to do more. We hope to do more. We call on all persons of good will to support us and lead, by making our system better than we have met it.
